title: Jude and the Contact
premise: Financial-crimes investigator Ines Ishikawa receives a calendar invitation from her former handler, Marcus Vane — sent hours after his confirmed death. The meeting pulls her into a covert network of 'cleaners' who launder the proceeds of a planned industrial sabotage in Frankfurt, disguised as an accident to trigger a market collapse. As Ines traces the money backward through shell companies and dead drops, she discovers the conspiracy reaches into the very agency that disowned her, and that Vane's death was the price of leaving a warning. With a makeshift team of outcasts she once investigated, she must expose and derail the attack before Frankfurt's markets open, choosing justice outside the law over the career that betrayed her. The book ends with the attack thwarted, the evidence released publicly, and Ines walking away from institutional power with her found family intact.
about_author: Theo Pemberton is a former compliance analyst who spent a decade tracing illicit finance across European markets before turning to fiction. He writes thrillers from a converted tram depot in Rotterdam, where he remains stubbornly anonymous about his sources.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.summary: Ines Ishikawa, buried in routine AML casework, receives a calendar invite from Marcus Vane — her old handler, declared dead two days ago. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: unease sharpening into compulsion; she cannot not go.

chapters.title: Clean Money
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: how Ines learned from Vane that the dirtiest money looks cleanest, and why she left the agency after he burned her last case. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: grief for a mentor and a self she abandoned.

chapters.title: Terminal 4, 6:40 AM
chapters.summary: Ines keeps the meeting at an airport café. Instead of Vane, a courier delivers a burner phone and a ledger fragment pointing to a Frankfurt logistics firm. She's photographed by someone who wants her involved. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: fear fused with exhilaration.

chapters.title: The Ledger Doesn't Lie
chapters.summary: Back at her desk, Ines quietly runs the ledger fragment: layered transfers through three shells, all converging on a date — the morning Frankfurt opens. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: investigator's cold clarity masking rising dread.

chapters.title: People Who Owe Me
chapters.summary: Ines recruits her first ally: Dov Reiner, a disgraced forensic accountant she once helped convict, now working pawn-shop books. He owes her and hates it. POV: Dov. Emotional beat: resentment thawing into wary loyalty.

chapters.title: Ghost Protocol
chapters.summary: The burner phone activates: a synthesized voice using Vane's cadence gives coordinates and one rule — trust no one inside the agency. Ines realizes the message was pre-scheduled by the dead man. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: mourning weaponized into purpose.

chapters.title: The Warehouse That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Surveillance of the logistics firm reveals a warehouse whose cargo manifests don't match its power draw — something energy-intensive is hidden inside. POV: Ines and alternating Dov. Emotional beat: the case stops being abstract.

chapters.title: Sable
chapters.summary: A second recruit: Sable Okonkwo, ex-military security consultant whom Ines once cleared of charges nobody else would touch. Sable agrees to breach the warehouse. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: a soldier without a war finding one worth fighting.

chapters.title: Inside the Draw
chapters.summary: Sable's covert entry finds server racks running a market-manipulation model and a schematic of Frankfurt's exchange cooling systems — the 'accident' will be a catastrophic failure blamed on infrastructure. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: cold horror at how tidy the plan is.

chapters.title: Who Signed Off
chapters.summary: Dov traces approvals on the shell companies to a dormant agency program — meaning insiders are laundering the operation's funding. Ines understands why Vane died. POV: Dov. Emotional beat: betrayal curdling into fury.

chapters.title: The Man from Oversight
chapters.summary: Agency official Aldous Krebs summons Ines, offers reinstatement if she hands over everything and forgets Frankfurt. She refuses; within hours her access is revoked and she's flagged. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: the door closing behind her — terror and freedom at once.

chapters.title: Fugitive Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Now officially rogue, the trio works from a safehouse. They map the full kill chain: fund the sabotage, short the market, blame a utility contractor. POV: rotating trio. Emotional beat: found family forming under pressure — bickering, shared meals, shared risk.

chapters.title: Vane's Dead Drop
chapters.summary: Following the phone's final instruction, Ines retrieves Vane's hidden cache: proof naming Krebs as architect, plus a letter apologizing for making her this way. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: forgiveness she can't deliver, resolve she can.

chapters.title: Counterparty
chapters.summary: They identify the saboteur cell's financier, a private bank fixer named Lenz, and flip him by threatening exposure of his own clients. First real win. POV: Dov. Emotional beat: the intoxication of leverage — and its taste of corruption.

chapters.title: Blowback
chapters.summary: Krebs strikes back: Sable is ambushed, the safehouse burned, and the media brands Ines a fugitive embezzler. The team scatters. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: cost made flesh; doubt whether any of this is survivable.

chapters.title: Low Point
chapters.summary: Hiding in Dov's cousin's basement, the team nearly fractures — Ines considers trading the cache for amnesty. Sable talks her back from it. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: despair answered by loyalty; the theme of justice beyond law crystallizes.

chapters.title: Forty-Eight Hours
chapters.summary: Countdown established: the sabotage is set for pre-market Friday. They reconstruct the plan from Lenz's records and decide they can't stop the physical attack — only make it meaningless. POV: rotating trio. Emotional beat: grim clarity; strategy replacing panic.

chapters.title: The Long Thursday
chapters.summary: Parallel operations: Sable shadows the saboteurs to confirm timing, Dov seeds the manipulation model with poisoned data, Ines prepares the public release. Each alone, each afraid. POV: all three, interleaved. Emotional beat: loneliness before the storm.

chapters.title: Frankfurt Opens
chapters.summary: Climax part one: the 'accident' occurs on schedule — but the poisoned data makes the shorts fail, and Ines livestreams Vane's cache mid-crash. Markets wobble but hold. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: terrifying public exposure; no way back.

chapters.title: Krebs Cornered
chapters.summary: Climax part two: confronted with his own signature in the ledger, Krebs attempts to destroy the servers and flee; Sable intercepts him at the exchange itself. He's arrested on camera — by the system he corrupted. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: justice done visibly, cathartically.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Inquiries begin; Ines negotiates immunity for her team by surrendering nothing but truth. Vane's letter finally read in full. The agency offers her old life back. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: quiet reckoning with what power costs.

chapters.title: What We Keep
chapters.summary: Epilogue: months later, the trio runs a small independent forensic consultancy from Rotterdam. A new anonymous invitation arrives. They look at each other — and say yes together. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: chosen family, chosen fight; the corruption of power met by people who refuse it.
